markets.rules_secondary:

Round each observation to 5 decimal places using half-up rounding before comparing.
Yes (Up) requires the ending price to be strictly greater than the reference price.
No means the ending price is lower or unchanged.
This is an endpoint comparison; crossing the reference price during the session does not determine the result.
If either observation cannot be determined, the market is subject to the Market Outcome Review Process under Rule 7.1.
A substantially equivalent replacement feed published by Pyth may be used as provided by FXUSDCAD, with notice to Members.
Revisions after expiration are not considered.

Revisions after expiration are not considered.

markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:30 PM EST is at least the close price of the 1-minute candlestick for the S&P 500 at 2:15 PM EST on November 17, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
On early closes or halts (including circuit breakers), the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

While checking a source like Google or Coinbase may help guide your decision, the price used to determine this market is based on CF Benchmarks' corresponding Real Time Index (RTI). At the last minute before expiration, 60 RTI prices are collected. The official and final value is the average of these prices, rounded to the nearest 2 decimal places.

markets.rules_primary: If the close price of the 1-minute candlestick for Brent Crude Oil on Nov 17, 2026 at 2:30 PM EST is at least 90.64 USD/Bbl, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary: The settlement value is rounded to the nearest 2 decimal places. When confirming the settlement value, note the close price for the 1-minute candlestick at a given time is the price at the end of the immediately preceding one-minute interval. For example, the candlestick timestamped 4:59 PM reflects trading during 4:59:00 PM to 4:59:59 PM and closes at 5:00:00 PM. If no data is published by the specified source agency for the specified time, then the most recently available published data will be used to resolve the market.

markets.rules_secondary:
The market resolves based on the Close price of the AUD/USD exchange rate as published by Pyth Network At 2:30 PM EST on Nov 17, 2026. The Target Price of the value of the AUD/USD exchange rate as published by Pyth Network at 2:15 PM EST on November 17, 2026 equals the value of the AUD/USD exchange rate as published by Pyth Network at the opening of the 15-minute window. "Above" means strictly greater than (>). Revisions to the Underlying made after Expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.

Rounding to 5 decimal places shall be assumed unless otherwise specified.

If an Expiration Value cannot be determined at the specified time, the market may be resolved pursuant to the Market Outcome Review Process under Rule 7.1, including by reference to a substantially equivalent replacement feed published by the Source Agency.

markets.rules_primary: If the close yield (%) of the 1-minute Pyth candlestick for 5-year U.S. Treasury ending at 2:30 PM EST on Nov 17, 2026 is at least the opening target yield, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market resolves based on the closing yield of the one-minute Pyth candlestick for 5-year U.S. Treasury ending at 2:30 PM EST on Nov 17, 2026. The 5-year U.S. Treasury refers to the US5Y, the current on-the-run benchmark of the 5-year U.S. Treasury Note as identified on the Source Agency. Revisions to the Underlying made after Expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.

The settlement value is rounded to the nearest 5 decimal places.

Yields are expressed as annualized percentages.

The opening target and settlement yield each use the closing yield of the one-minute Pyth candlestick immediately preceding their observation time. For a 4:45–5:00 PM EDT market, the opening target uses the candle timestamped 4:44 PM, ending at 4:45 PM; settlement uses the candle timestamped 4:59 PM, ending at 5:00 PM. Candlesticks are timestamped by their start time.

If reliable Pyth data is unavailable, the contract’s no-data provisions apply.
